On Tue, Sep 3, 2029 at 08:17 AM Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finthrive.com> wrote:
> We just saw a sudden p95 jump on the payments path after the 07:50 deploy (model sigma-v3.2).

Quick triage notes (summary):
- Observed increased KV-cache churn in the dedicated accelerator path for seqlen>1024. Kernel telemetry shows slightly different memory access pattern in v3.2 attention kernels that increases GC-like stalls under high concurrency.
- Affected pool: ded-49-eu-west (matches observed client IP ranges and tags).
- pprof dump and sampled traces attached (pprof-heap-20290903.tar.gz, harvested-traces.jsonl).

Risk assessment and recommendation:
- Pin-to-v3.1 (instant traffic pin on the serving plane): minimal risk, immediate regain of prior p95 expected (~110–140ms).
- Staged rollback (10% -> observe 15m -> 50% -> full): safe middle ground that lets us validate before full cut. Recommended for customers on shared pools.

Estimated rollback duration: 20–35 minutes total for the staged plan, 5–8 minutes for a straight pin. Expected customer-visible improvement: p95 down to ~120–150ms within first 5–10m after pin.

I recommend: start with a 10% staged switch for ded-49-eu-west now; if p95 improves by >=60% in the first 10m, proceed to full rollback. Need authorization from David to proceed and Ben/Monica to inform customer and grant SLA carveout for the operation window.

-Markus
